title: Thai massaman chicken curry with potatoes
blurb: Sweet, mellow and nutty, with tender chicken, soft potato and a tamarind tang over jasmine rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat and fry the onion wedges for 4 minutes until they start to colour. Stir in the massaman paste and star anise and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste for 2 minutes, then pour in the coconut milk and {ml 150} of water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato, tamarind, fish sauce and sugar. Simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft and the sauce has thickened and glossy.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Toast the peanuts in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until golden, then roughly crush them.
Taste the curry and add a splash more fish sauce or a pinch more sugar if it needs it. Spoon it over the rice and top with the peanuts and {coriander}.

title: Holy basil chicken with a crispy fried egg
blurb: Fiery minced chicken wok-fried with garlic and basil, piled on rice under a lacy-edged fried egg.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce and sugar with {ml 30} of water in a small bowl.

Heat {ml 15} of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add the garlic and {chilli} and stir-fry for 20 seconds, then add the chicken and break it up. Fry hard for 4–5 minutes until golden in places and cooked through.
Add the green beans and the sauce and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the beans are just tender and the sauce clings. Take off the heat and stir through most of the basil until it wilts.
Wipe out the pan, heat the remaining oil over a high heat and fry the eggs for 2 minutes until the whites are crisp and bubbly at the edges with the yolks still runny.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the chicken and a fried egg, and scatter over the remaining basil.

title: Larb-style pork in lettuce cups
blurb: Zingy minced pork with lime, mint and toasted rice powder, scooped up in crisp {little gem} leaves.
steps: Toast the rice in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5–6 minutes, shaking often, until deep golden. Tip it into a mortar or bowl and crush it to a coarse powder with a pestle or the base of a rolling pin.
Heat the oil in the same pan over a high heat. Add the pork and fry for 6–7 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through and lightly browned.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the juice of {qty 1.5|lime|limes}, the fish sauce, sugar and {chilli flakes}, then fold in the shallots, toasted rice powder, mint, {coriander} and {spring onions}.
Taste and add more lime or fish sauce so it is sharp, salty and hot. Cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Pile the warm pork into the {little gem} leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

title: Mushroom tom kha-style coconut soup
blurb: A fragrant coconut broth with lemongrass, lime leaf and ginger, loaded with mushrooms, tofu and noodles.
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Fry the mushrooms for 5 minutes until they release their water and start to brown.
Add the lemongrass, ginger, lime leaves and half the {chilli}, and cook for 1 minute. Crumble in the {stock cube}, then pour in the coconut milk and {ml 500} of water.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes so the aromatics flavour the broth. Do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.
Add the tofu, soy sauce and sugar and simmer for 3 minutes. Meanwhile, soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 5 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain.

Squeeze in the juice of the lime, then taste and adjust with more soy or sugar. Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the soup and top with the {spring onions}, {coriander} and remaining {chilli}.
Leave the lemongrass, ginger and lime leaves at the side of the bowl; they flavour the soup but are not for eating.

title: Pad see ew with tofu, egg and tenderstem
blurb: Wide rice noodles charred in a hot pan with sweet soy, scrambled egg and crisp tenderstem.

ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into {cm 2} cubes

steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 6–8 minutes, or as the packet says, until pliable but still firm. Drain well and toss with {ml 15} of the oil so they do not stick.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar and black pepper with {ml 30} of water in a small bowl.
Heat {ml 30} of the oil in a large frying pan or wok over a high heat. Fry the tofu for 5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides, then lift it onto a plate.
Add the garlic and tenderstem to the pan with a splash of water and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Push to one side, then pour the eggs into the gap and scramble for 30 seconds until just set.
Add the noodles, tofu and sauce. Toss and press the noodles against the pan for 2–3 minutes, turning, until they take on some charred spots and are coated in the sauce.
Serve straight away with the lime wedges.

title: Jungle curry-style vegetable curry
blurb: A hot, thin, coconut-free curry packed with {aubergine}, beans and basil, as fiery and herby as it gets.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the curry paste, lemongrass and half the {chilli} for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until the oil turns red and the paste smells toasted.
Add the {aubergine} and stir for 3 minutes, then pour in {ml 600} of water, crumble in the {stock cube} and add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.

Bring to the boil, then simmer for 8 minutes. Add the carrot and {courgette} and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans for 4 minutes more, until everything is tender but the beans still have a bite.
Stir in most of the basil and squeeze in half the lime. Taste; it should be hot, salty and a little sweet.
Ladle into bowls over the rice, topping with the remaining basil and {chilli} and a wedge of the remaining lime.

title: Thai fish cakes with cucumber salad and sweet {chilli} dip
blurb: Bouncy, spiced white fish patties fried until golden, with a cool cucumber salad and rice.

ingredients.prep: central stems removed, very finely shredded

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with {g 1} of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Blitz the fish with the curry paste, egg, {cornflour} and fish sauce in a food processor until it forms a thick, sticky paste, scraping down once. Stir in the green beans and lime leaves.
Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, sugar and the remaining salt and leave to sit. Mix the sweet {chilli} sauce with a squeeze of lime juice and half the {coriander}.
With wet hands, shape the fish mixture into 8 flat patties about {cm 1.5} thick.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the cakes in 2 batches for 3 minutes on each side until deep golden and cooked through, then drain on {kitchen paper}.
Serve the fish cakes with the rice, cucumber salad and dip, sprinkled with the remaining {coriander} and lime wedges from the remaining lime.

title: Panang-style chicken curry
blurb: A thick, rich and lightly sweet red curry with peanut butter, lime leaf and crisp-tender peppers.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.

Spoon about a third of the coconut milk, the thick part from the top of the tin, into a wide pan over a medium heat with the oil. Fry the curry paste in it for 2 minutes, stirring, until it splits and smells fragrant.
Stir in the peanut butter, then add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes, turning, until the outside turns white.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, then add the fish sauce, sugar and lime leaves. Simmer gently for 8 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Add the {red pepper} and green beans and simmer for 4 minutes until crisp-tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste and balance with more fish sauce or sugar. Serve over the rice topped with the basil.

title: Khao soi-style curry noodles with crispy tofu
blurb: Silky turmeric coconut broth over egg noodles, with crisp tofu, quick pickled onion and {chilli} oil.

ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into {cm 2} cubes

steps: Toss the red onion with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of the sugar and leave to pickle while you cook.
Heat {ml 20} of the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan with the curry paste, curry powder, turmeric, ginger and garlic. Fry for 1–2 minutes over a medium heat, stirring, until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and {ml 300} of water, crumble in the {stock cube} and add the soy sauce and the rest of the sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling water for 3–4 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain well.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with the tofu, pickled onion, {spring onions}, {coriander} and a drizzle of {chilli} oil. Serve with wedges of the remaining lime.

title: Thai cashew chicken stir-fry
blurb: Glossy, savoury-sweet chicken with toasted cashews, peppers and {spring onions}, ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Toss the chicken with the {cornflour}. Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar and {chilli flakes} with {ml 60} of water.
Toast the cashews in a dry wok or large frying pan over a medium heat for 2–3 minutes until golden, then tip them out.
Heat the oil in the pan over a high heat. Fry the chicken for 4 minutes, turning, until golden. Add the onion, {red pepper}, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes until it thickens and coats everything, then stir in the cashews and {spring onions}.
Serve straight away over the rice.

title: Crispy tofu and green bean red curry
blurb: Golden {cornflour}-crusted tofu and snappy beans in a creamy, {chilli}-warm red coconut sauce.

ingredients.prep: pressed dry and cut into {cm 2} cubes

steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with {g 1} of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.

Toss the tofu with the {cornflour} and the rest of the salt until evenly coated. Heat {ml 30} of the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out onto a plate.
In a wide pan, heat the remaining oil over a medium heat and fry the curry paste for 1–2 minutes until fragrant. Pour in the coconut milk and add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans and {red pepper} and cook for 5–6 minutes until just tender.
Fold the crispy tofu into the sauce, squeeze in half the lime and taste for balance. Serve over the rice with the basil and wedges from the remaining lime.

title: Thai {prawn} fried rice with egg and lime
blurb: Wok-hot rice with juicy {prawns}, egg and garlic, finished with cool cucumber, tomato and lime.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Spread it on a tray and leave to cool and dry out for 10 minutes; cold rice fries far better than steaming-hot rice.
Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar and black pepper in a small bowl.
Heat {ml 15} of the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Fry the {prawns} for 2 minutes until pink, then tip them onto a plate.

Add the remaining oil and fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the garlic, {chilli} and the white parts of the {spring onions} for 30 seconds. Push to the side, crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and sauce and stir-fry hard for 3–4 minutes, breaking up any lumps. Return the {prawns} and toss for 1 minute.
Serve topped with the tomato, cucumber, {coriander} and the green parts of the {spring onions}, with the lime wedges for squeezing.

title: Butternut squash and chickpea Thai green curry
blurb: Sweet roast-soft squash and spinach in a fragrant green coconut curry, bulked out with chickpeas.
steps: Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium heat. Fry the green paste for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the squash and stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk and {ml 150} of water. Add the lime leaves, soy sauce and sugar.
Simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir in the chickpeas and cook for 3 minutes, then add the spinach and stir until wilted, about 1 minute.
Squeeze in half the lime and taste for salt, sweetness and sourness. Serve over the rice with the basil and wedges from the remaining lime.

title: Thai-style steak salad with lime, mint and {chilli}
blurb: Seared sliced steak tossed with crunchy cucumber, tomato and herbs in a hot, sour, salty dressing.
steps: Pat the steak dry and season both sides with the salt and black pepper.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat until almost smoking. Sear the steak for 2–3 minutes on each side for medium-rare, longer if you prefer it more done, then rest it on a board for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the juice of {qty 2|lime|limes} with the fish sauce, sugar and half the {chilli} until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, mint and {coriander} in a large bowl with most of the dressing.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and toss it gently with the salad and the juices from the board.
Arrange the {little gem} leaves on plates, pile the salad on top, spoon over the remaining dressing and scatter with the remaining {chilli}.

title: Shaking beef with peppery lime dip and {rocket}
blurb: Seared garlicky beef cubes, shaken in a hot pan, with a salt-and-pepper lime dip and peppery leaves.
steps: Toss the beef with half the garlic, the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, half the sugar and {g 1} of the black pepper. Leave to marinate for 15 minutes while you cook the rice.
Rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with {g 1} of the salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
For the dip, mix the juice of {qty 1|lime|limes} with {g 1} of the salt and the remaining black pepper in a small bowl, stirring until the salt dissolves.

Heat half the oil in a large frying pan or wok over the highest heat you have. Sear the beef in 2 batches for 2 minutes each, shaking the pan and turning the cubes, until browned outside and pink within. Tip onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the onion wedges and the rest of the garlic and sugar and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the onion has charred edges. Return the beef and toss for 30 seconds.
Toss the {rocket} and tomatoes with a squeeze of the remaining lime. Serve the beef over the leaves with the rice, the lime dip for dunking and the lime wedges.

title: Vietnamese caramel pork with eggs and {pak choi}
blurb: Pork braised in a dark, glossy caramel of fish sauce and pepper, with soft eggs and rice.
steps: Lower the eggs into a pan of boiling water and cook for 7 minutes, then cool under cold running water and peel.
Put the sugar and {ml 30} of water in a heavy pan over a medium heat without stirring. Cook for 5–6 minutes until it turns a deep amber, swirling the pan, then take it off the heat.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the pork for 5 minutes until browned, then add the shallots, garlic and ginger for 1 minute.

Add the caramel, the fish sauce, black pepper and {ml 250} of water. Bring to a simmer, add the peeled eggs and simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, turning the pork and eggs now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick and sticky.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the salt for 12 minutes. Steam the {pak choi} in a covered pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes until just tender.
Halve the eggs and serve the pork and sauce with the rice and {pak choi}, topped with the {chilli} and {spring onions}.

title: Chicken phở-style noodle soup
blurb: A clear, star anise and ginger broth with poached chicken, rice noodles, bean sprouts and plenty of herbs.
steps: Put the onion halves cut-side down and the ginger in a dry saucepan over a high heat. Char for 4–5 minutes until blackened in places, then add the star anise and cinnamon and toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in {ml 1000} of water, crumble in the {stock cubes} and add the fish sauce, sugar and black pepper. Bring to the boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Slide in the chicken breasts and poach for 14–16 minutes until cooked through with no pink in the middle. Lift out onto a board and rest for 5 minutes, then shred or slice.
Simmer the broth for another 5 minutes, then strain it through a sieve back into the pan, discarding the aromatics, and keep it hot.
Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 4–5 minutes, or as the packet says, then drain and divide between deep bowls.
Top the noodles with the chicken and ladle over the boiling-hot broth. Serve with the bean sprouts, {spring onions}, {coriander}, basil, {chilli} and lime wedges for everyone to add at the table.

title: Beef rendang-style coconut curry
blurb: Beef simmered until tender in a dry, sticky, deeply spiced coconut and lemongrass sauce.
steps: Blitz the shallots, garlic, ginger and {chilli} with the ground {coriander}, cumin, turmeric and cinnamon and {ml 30} of water in a small blender or processor to a rough paste.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over a medium heat. Fry the paste for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and the raw smell goes.
Add the beef and turn it in the paste for 3 minutes. Pour in the coconut milk and {ml 100} of water, then add the lemongrass, lime leaves, tamarind, sugar, soy sauce and {g 1} of the salt.
Bring to a simmer and cook gently, uncovered, for 40–45 minutes, stirring every 5–10 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and simmer it covered in {ml 300} of water with the remaining salt for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered.
For the last 10 minutes, raise the heat slightly and stir often as the sauce reduces to a thick, dark coating that clings to the beef. Remove the lemongrass and lime leaves and serve with the rice.
